s: Mega Food Parks scheme has been initiated by the Government of India with the objective :
o: To improve infrastructure facilities for food processing
To increase productivity of food crops
x: The Scheme of Mega Food Park has been initiated for providing a mechanism to link agricultural production to the market by bringing together farmers, processors and retailers so as to ensure maximizing value addition, minimizing wastage, increasing farmers' income and creating employment opportunities particularly in rural sector. The Mega Food Park Scheme was based on 'Cluster' approach and envisages creation of state of art support infrastructure in a welldefined agri/horticultural zone for setting up of modern food processing units in the industrial plots provided in the park with well-established supply chain. Mega food park typically consisted of supply chain infrastructure including collection centers, primary processing centers, central processing centers, cold chain and around 25-30 fully developed plots for entrepreneurs to set up food processing units. This Scheme has been discontinued by the Government with effect from 1 April, 2021 with provision for committed liabilities for ongoing projects only.

s: As per the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, which of the following mark is made mandatory on all processed fruit products sold in our country?
x: The Food Products Order (FPO) mark is a mandatory certification mark for all processed fruit products sold in India, such as fruit jams, packaged fruit beverages, crushes and squashes, dehydrated fruit products, pickles, and fruit extracts. The FPO mark guarantees that the food products are manufactured in a hygienic and food-safe environment, ensuring that the product is fit for consumption. The Ministry of Food Processing Industries develops food safety hygiene standards and issues the FPO mark certification to processed food manufacturers. In India, the FPO certificate has been effective since the promulgation of Food Products Order 1955, but it became mandatory for manufacturers only after the enactment of the Food Safety and Standards (FSS) Act, 2006.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Karnataka is the leading state in mulberry silk. Jharkhand leads in tasar, while Assam leads in muga and eri silk.

s: Through which body does the National Beekeeping and Honey Mission, launched in 2020, implement the Sweet Revolution?
x: The National Beekeeping and Honey Mission implements the Sweet Revolution through the National Bee Board.

s: India is the only country producing all five commercial silks. Which of these is NOT among them?
x: The five commercial silks are mulberry, tropical tasar, oak tasar, eri and muga; Merino is not a silk.

s: Which of the following pairs of silk and leading State is correctly matched?
x: Tasar is led by Jharkhand, mulberry by Karnataka, and muga and eri by Assam.

s: After Andhra Pradesh, which State is the next largest egg producer?
x: Andhra Pradesh is the top egg State, followed by Tamil Nadu.

s: What is the position of Andhra Pradesh in terms of the length of coast line in the country?

The second fastest growing economy in the world is:
What is Andhra Pradesh's rank among States in milk production?
x: AP is seventh in milk production (India is first); its principal national lead is in aquaculture.

s: Which is the largest and fastest-growing allied sub-sector in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Fisheries is AP's largest and fastest-growing allied sub-sector, with 17.69% growth.

s: As per the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26, how much area did horticulture cover in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Survey reported horticulture over 46.43 lakh acres with production of 406.38 lakh MT.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's rank in coconut production?
x: Andhra Pradesh is 4th in coconut production. It is 1st in oil palm (2.27 lakh ha), so do not confuse the two rankings.

s:
Consider the following about Andhra Pradesh:
1. It is the largest producer of aquaculture and farmed shrimp in India.
2. Vannamei is its predominant farmed shrimp variety.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: AP is India's largest aquaculture and farmed-shrimp producer, and Vannamei is the predominant variety.

s: What is Andhra Pradesh's rank among Indian States in raw silk production (2024-25)?
x: AP is the 2nd largest raw silk producer (61,394 MT of cocoons in 2024-25), with its belt around Hindupur (Sri Sathya Sai/Anantapur) and Chittoor. India as a whole is also 2nd in the world. First, third and fifth are wrong.

s: Which of the following crops or products is NOT included among the horticultural activities identified for the development of Rayalaseema as a horticulture hub?
x: The identified activities include banana, oil palm, cashew, coconut and Araku coffee. Tea is not included in that list.

s: Which area forms the main sericulture belt of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Sri Sathya Sai/Anantapur around Hindupur and Chittoor
x: The principal sericulture belt lies in Sri Sathya Sai/Anantapur, particularly around Hindupur, and in Chittoor.

s: At what rate did fishing and aquaculture, Andhra Pradesh's largest allied sub-sector, grow?
x: Fishing and aquaculture is AP's largest and fastest-growing allied sub-sector at 17.69%.

s: For which crop is Araku Valley in Andhra Pradesh known?
x: Araku is known for coffee, not tea.

s: In which of the following does Andhra Pradesh rank first in India?
x: AP is 1st in oil palm (2.27 lakh ha); it is 7th in milk, 4th in coconut and 2nd in raw silk.

s: Which district is the top dairy district of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Chittoor is AP's top dairy district.

s: From which place are Andhra Pradesh's banana exports to the Gulf sent by refrigerated trains?
x: About 32,000 MT of bananas went to the Gulf by 8 refrigerated trains from Tadipatri.

s: The country, which is the largest silk producer in the world, is :
x: China is the world's largest silk producer, with India second. India is notable only as the one country producing all five commercial silks.

s: Which of the following countries is the largest producer of fish in the world?
x: As per FAO's 'The State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture (SOFIA) 2024', China is the largest and main producer of both capture fisheries and aquaculture. In 2022, China remained the first major producer with a share of 36 percent of the world's total aquatic animal production, followed by India (8%) and Indonesia (7%). In addition to being by far the major fish producer, China has also been the main exporter of fish and fish products since 2002.

s: What is India's position in global milk production and its approximate share of world output?
x: India is the world's number-one milk producer and accounts for approximately 25 per cent of global milk output.

s: India occupies which position in the production of silk, and what distinction is associated with its silk production?
o: First; it produces only one variety of silk

Second; it produces only the mulberry variety
Third; it is the only country producing three varieties of silk
x: India is the second-largest silk producer and is identified as the only country producing all five varieties of silk.

s: Which of the following animals are classified as small ruminants?
x: Small ruminants are sheep and goats; cattle and buffalo are large ruminants, and horses, donkeys, pigs and rabbits are not ruminants. (Off-topic animal-husbandry question, moved.)

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Match the animals with their delivery process
x: Cows calve, ewes lamb, goats kid and dogs whelp, so Cow-Calving, Sheep-Lambing, Goat-Kidding, Dog-Whelping. Off-topic, moved to animal husbandry.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Ranikhet disease in birds is manifested by
x: Ranikhet (Newcastle) disease of poultry shows respiratory signs (gasping), nervous signs (twisted neck, paralysis) and gastrointestinal signs (greenish diarrhoea), so all of these. Off-topic, moved.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Which of the following is an example for small size dog breed
x: The pug is a toy (small) dog breed; the boxer and Dalmatian are large breeds and the bulldog is medium.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Which of the following is used to induce epidural anaesthesia in cows
x: Lignocaine (lidocaine, 2%) is the standard local anaesthetic for caudal epidural anaesthesia in cattle; thiopentone and propofol are general anaesthetics and morphine an opioid.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Falling out of any part of the womb of pregnant cattle either before or after calving is called as
x: The falling out of the uterus (or vagina) of a pregnant or calving cow is called prolapse; pyometra is pus in the uterus, perimetritis inflammation around it, and involution its return to normal size.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Duration of oestrous period in buffaloes in hours
x: Oestrus (heat) in buffaloes lasts about 24-36 hours, longer than in cows (about 18 h). Off-topic (animal husbandry).

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: The shelf life of canned meat products is
x: Properly processed and stored canned (heat-sterilised) meat products keep for about two years; standard meat-technology texts give 2 years as the shelf life.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: What is the optimum service period in a cross-bred cow for profitable dairying
x: For profitable dairying a cross-bred cow should be served again within about 60-90 days (≈3 months) of calving, giving a calving interval of about 12-13 months.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: In the slaughter house the gradient of the floor should be
x: Slaughter-house floors are laid with a fall of about 1 in 48 to 1 in 60 towards the drains, i.e. about 2 cm per metre; 0.5 cm/m is too flat to drain and 4-5 cm/m too steep and slippery for workers and animals.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: First scientific artificial insemination was performed by
x: Italian scientist Lazzaro Spallanzani performed the first scientific artificial insemination, in a dog, in 1780. Ivanoff (Russia, early 1900s) developed it for livestock; Sampath Kumaran pioneered it in India (1939, Mysore).

s: Where is the ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (ICAR-IIHR), located, which organised the 'National Horticultural Fair-2023' during 22 - 25 February 2023
x: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research is at Hesaraghatta, Bengaluru (Karnataka); it hosted the National Horticultural Fair 2023.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: The time and temperature used in HTST pasteurisation
x: HTST pasteurisation heats milk to about 72°C for 15 seconds; 63°C for 30 minutes is the batch (LTLT) method.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: First artificial insemination was performed in India at
x: India's first artificial insemination of cattle was done in 1939 at the Palace Dairy Farm, Mysore (by Sampath Kumaran); Izzatnagar is the IVRI seat. (Off-topic; moved.)

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Hatching eggs can be better stored up to
x: Hatching eggs keep their hatchability best when set within about 7 days of laying (stored cool, about 13-16 °C); hatchability falls quickly after a week. An animal-husbandry question, moved.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Floor space required usually per hen for raising layer hens in deep litter system
x: Layer hens on deep litter usually need about 2 sq ft of floor space per bird (1 sq ft is for growers, 0.5 for chicks). (Animal husbandry; moved.)

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: The minimum number of turnings required in setter per day
x: Eggs in a setter (incubator) should be turned at least 6–8 times a day to stop the embryo sticking to the shell membrane.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: What is the presence of pus in the uterus called?
x: Pyometra is a collection of pus in the uterus; endometritis is inflammation of the uterine lining.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s: What grazing management practice involves moving livestock through six or more paddocks in sequence several times during the season?
x: Moving livestock through a sequence of paddocks during the season, so each rests and regrows, is rotational grazing; leader-follower and creep grazing are special forms.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: In artificial incubation when the eggs are transferred from setter to hatcher
x: Chicken eggs take 21 days to hatch; in artificial incubation they are moved from the setter to the hatcher on the 18th day, when turning stops.
